what: HyperGAT: document-level hypergraphs with dual attention
title: Benchmarks: R8, R52, MR, Ohsumed, 20NG
text: hg_hypergat() implements Ding et al. (2020) natively: every document becomes hypergraph (unique words vertices, sentences hyperedges), first attention layer aggregates words sentence representations, second aggregates sentences back words, masked mean pool feeds classifier. implementation mirrors official code (verified source, forward-pass parity float32 precision). semantic = "none" uses sentence hyperedges alone; semantic = "lda" adds paper’s online-LDA topic hyperedges, trained labeled documents , precomputed official keyword lists can passed replay upstream preprocessing boundary exactly. benchmark table predates implementation remains explicitly sentence-, closest published comparator paper’s “w/o semantic” ablation. One honest difference: official preprocessing lemmatizes WordNet; . benchmark runs official repository’s corpus files (TextGCN cleaned files used contain sentence punctuation ), whose R8 split 5,501/2,190 rather TextGCN’s 5,485/2,189. Official training protocol throughout: 10 epochs, batch 8, StepLR, balanced class weights, 10% validation checkpointing; three torch seeds. Every row run semantic = "none", set beside published ablation also drops semantic hyperedges: package’s strongest result. R8 reaches 0.9665 (SD 0.0034) – every method article, 0.49 points matching published ablation, HyperGAT w/o semantic (0.9714 +/- 0.0026), near published transductive TextGCN (0.9707). R52 reaches 0.9433 (SD 0.0018), 0.18 points published w/o-semantic ablation (0.9415 +/- 0.0032) published transductive TextGCN (0.9356) – previous R52 best 0.8797 (centroid). Full HyperGAT (0.9797 R8, 0.9498 R52) adds LDA semantic hyperedges runs use, like--like comparator. Wall-clock: four minutes per training run laptop CPU. architecture, optimization corpus-level design, skewed news corpora needed.
code: hypergat <- read.csv("benchmark-hypergat.csv") knitr::kable(hypergat, digits = 4) ablation <- subset(published, model == "HyperGAT w/o semantic",                    select = c(dataset, accuracy, sd)) full <- with(subset(published, model == "HyperGAT"),              data.frame(dataset, full_hypergat = accuracy)) comparison <- merge(   subset(hypergat, semantic == "none", select = c(dataset, accuracy, sd)),   ablation, by = "dataset", suffixes = c("_ours", "_wo_semantic") ) comparison <- merge(comparison, full, by = "dataset") comparison <- transform(comparison,                         difference = accuracy_ours - accuracy_wo_semantic) knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 4)

code: library(hypernets)  # memory network: what follows what, given how you got here net <- hon(human_long, action = "code", actor = "session_id",            time = "timestamp", max_order = 3) hg_centrality(net, sort_by = "pagerank")  # simplicial complex: the same sessions as a pathway complex sc <- simplicial(net, type = "pathway") hg_betti(sc)  # hypergraph: each session as one multi-way interaction over its codes hg <- group_hypergraph(human_long, actor = "code", group = "session_id") hg_centrality(hg, type = "pagerank")  # text: a corpus as a document-word hypergraph, clustered into topics thg <- text_hypergraph(covid_abstracts, column = "abstract", id = "doc",                        weight = "tfidf", stop_words = stop_words_en(),                        min_count = 3L) topics <- hg_cluster(thg, k = 4, type = "random_walk", seed = 1) hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, collapse = TRUE)                    # tf-idf mass hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "ctfidf", collapse = TRUE)  # BERTopic's c-TF-IDF hg_keywords(thg, topics, n = 5, type = "centrality", collapse = TRUE)

title: Hypergraph eigenvector centralities — hg_centrality.net_hg
text: hypergraph method hg_centrality(). Computes one eigenvector-style centralities net_hg: clique-motif (CEC), Z-eigenvector (ZEC), H-eigenvector (HEC). variant captures influence differently - CEC flattens group structure via clique expansion, ZEC HEC propagate higher-order groups directly.

PageRank damping factor (probability following walk rather teleporting). Default 0.85. used type = "pagerank". edge_weights NULL, single positive number (recycled every hyperedge, e.g. 1 unit weights), positive numeric vector, one per hyperedge. Hyperedge weights EDVW random walk behind type = "pagerank"; NULL defaults window counts hypergraphs built window_hypergraph(), else Hayashi et al. dispersion heuristic (unit weights binary incidence). used type = "pagerank". alpha Attenuation factor type = "katz": single number \((0, 1/\lambda_{max})\), \(\lambda_{max}\) largest eigenvalue hypergraph adjacency. correct default; type = "katz" without alpha raises hypernets_bad_input, alpha bound (message reports ). ... text:
type also accepts "pagerank" (EDVW hypergraph PageRank), "subhypergraph" "katz" (Katz centrality, needs alpha); result one row per node. Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC): forms clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) \(W_{ij} = |\{e : , j \e\}|\) returns leading eigenvector \(W\). Equivalent running igraph::eigen_centrality() hg_clique_expansion() output. Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC): solves linear eigen-equation hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j,$$ via power iteration. Works hypergraphs mixed edge sizes. H-eigenvector centrality (HEC): solves power-k-1 eigen-equation, $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j.$$ uniform hypergraphs (hyperedges size \(k\)), equivalent normalizing ZEC update geometric-mean exponent \(1/(k-1)\). mixed sizes, effective exponent taken largest hyperedge; expect slightly different rankings ZEC mixed case. Hypergraph PageRank ("pagerank"): stationary distribution damped EDVW random walk Chitra & Raphael (2019): node \(v\), pick hyperedge \(e 
i v\) probability proportional weight \(w(e)\), node \(u \e\) probability proportional edge-dependent vertex weight \(\gamma_e(u)\) (incidence cell, .e. occurrence totals window_hypergraph()); probability \(1 - damping\) teleport uniformly. collapse theorem: edge-independent vertex weights (binary incidence) walk equivalent PageRank weighted clique expansion edge weights \(\sum_{e 
i u,v} w(e)/\delta(e)\) – hypergraph adds information exactly \(\gamma\) edge-dependent. Nodes left hyperedge (possible min_weight/min_size filtering) teleport every step receive teleportation mass. undamped stationary distribution walk pi column reported hg_cluster(). Subhypergraph centrality ("subhypergraph"): logarithm diagonal matrix exponential clique adjacency derived binary incidence (entries count shared hyperedges), \(\log[\exp(W)]_{ii}\). counts closed walks based node factorial penalty length matches implementation used HypergraphX 1.5 legal-hypergraphs analysis. Katz centrality ("katz"): Katz's (1953) status index hypergraph adjacency Estrada & Rodriguez-Velazquez (2006), \(A_{ij}\) = number hyperedges containing \(\) \(j\) (weighted clique expansion), $$x = \sum_{k \ge 1} \alpha^k ^k \mathbf{1} = (- \alpha )^{-1} \alpha \mathbf{1},\qquad 0 < \alpha < 1/\lambda_{max}(),$$ \(\alpha\)-discounted number walks leaving node (Battiston et al. 2020, Sec. III.B.3). Returned natural scale, normalized; alpha centrality Bonacich & Lloyd (2001) unit exogenous status, also counts length-0 walk, katz + 1 (tested igraph::alpha_centrality() clique expansion). XGI's katz_centrality() vector fixed \(\alpha = 2^{-n}\), rescaled sum one (tested). type also runs sparse incidence.

text: memory-network method hg_centrality(). Computes centralities higher-order topology hon() network , default, projects back onto first-order states, following Scholtes, Wider & Garas (2016). higher-order node carries memory state reached, centralities can rank states differently measures first-order transition network - difference evidence memory matters flow, just prediction.

title: Higher-order centralities with first-order projection — hg_centrality.net_hon
text: x net_hon object hon(). type Character vector, subset c("pagerank", "betweenness", "closeness"). Default computes three. project Logical. TRUE (default) returns one row per first-order state; FALSE returns one row per higher-order node ordinary directed-graph centralities higher-order topology (useful see contexts, states, dominate). projection higher-order node's PageRank distributed states path project = TRUE: "scaled" (default, pathpy's default - k states receives k-th value, projected PageRank still sums 1), "last" (state actually occupied), "first", "" (every state path receives full value; result longer sums 1). Ignored betweenness closeness, first-order construction. damping PageRank damping factor (0, 1). Default 0.85. weighted Logical. FALSE (default, pathpy's convention) runs PageRank binary higher-order topology; TRUE uses edge weights hon$matrix. max_iter, tol Power-iteration controls PageRank. max_paths Integer cap shortest paths enumerated betweenness. Exceeding raises hypernets_too_many_paths error rather silently truncating. Default 1e6. sort_by NULL (alphabetical state node, default) one requested types - sort table centrality, largest first, ties broken state/node order stays deterministic. top Integer NULL. Return first top rows, applied filter sort_by, sort_by top compose. Default NULL returns every row. ... Must empty: argument hypergraph method takes raises hypernets_bad_input.

text: Projects net_hg standard pairwise netobject (clique expansion - also called "downgrade" hypergraph dyadic graph). hyperedge size k contributes 1 (weight) every pair members. resulting edge weight W[, j] equals number hyperedges containing j (binary incidence) sum incidence products (weighted incidence).

title: Clique expansion of a hypergraph — hg_clique_expansion
text: netobject (also cograph_network) method = "hg_clique_expansion", undirected, weighted symmetric adjacency W = incidence %*% t(incidence) zero diagonal.

title: Clique expansion of a hypergraph — hg_clique_expansion
text: clique expansion standard "loss-y lossless--pairwise" projection: preserves pairs co-occurred often discards higher-order grouping. Comparing hg_clique_expansion(hg) directly-estimated pairwise co-occurrence network data quantifies much information carried hyperedge structure. Computed one BLAS call via tcrossprod(incidence); runs O(n_nodes^2 * n_hyperedges) time, fast typical sizes. Closes /O cycle: event data -> group_hypergraph() -> hg_clique_expansion() -> function accepts netobject (centrality, bootstrap, clustering, plotting via cograph).

(2023), gives every node membership vector k communities likelihood model whole hypergraph. weight \(A_e\) hyperedge \(e\) Poisson mean \(\lambda_e / \kappa_{|e|}\), $$\lambda_e = \sum_{< j \e} u_i^\top w\, u_j,$$ \(u\) non-negative \(N \times k\) membership matrix, \(w\) symmetric non-negative \(k \times k\) affinity communities \(\kappa_n = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\binom{N-2}{n-2}\) normalises size \(n\) hyperedge. title: Degree-preserving null-model test of hypergraph structure — hg_null_test
text: hg text_hypergraph(), knn_hypergraph(), hypernets net_hg. statistic Statistics test; "pairwise_participation", "density", "avg_edge_size", "avg_jaccard" (mean pairwise edge Jaccard), "repeated_edges" (hyperedges whose member set already occurred: paper's repeated collaboration trios) "repeated_pairs" (member pairs counted multiplicity minus distinct co-occurring pairs: repeated collaboration pairs). Several allowed. method null. "swap" (default) checkerboard swap chain : margins preserved exactly, vertex may repeat within hyperedge. "configuration" draws independent stub-matchings (Chodrow 2020), standard higher-order configuration model: vertex stubs matched uniformly random hyperedge slots, margins hold collapse (vertex whose stubs land twice one hyperedge loses degree). "assignment" degree-ordered assignment Coupette et al. (2024) use repeated-collaboration test: vertices decreasing degree choose hyperedges without replacement among free slot, margins hold exactly vertex repeats within hyperedge, price draw uniform configurations. "swap" stricter null; use "configuration" compare higher-order network literature, reports . n Number null samples (default 199L). seed Seed null draws; set reproducible test. global RNG state restored exit. alternative "two_sided" (default), "greater", "less".

title: Local clustering coefficients of a hypergraph — hg_transitivity
text: "projection" – Watts & Strogatz (1998) local clustering unweighted clique expansion: share pairs node's neighbours neighbours. path hyperedges closed hyperedge, single hyperedge size three already closes triangle (path-based generalization reviewed Battiston et al. 2020, Sec. III.C). "extra_overlap" – Zhou & Nakhleh (2011), statement Klimm, Deane & Reinert (2021): every unordered pair hyperedges \(e,   f\) containing node, extra overlap $$EO(e, f) = \frac{|N(D_{e,f}) \cap D_{f,e}| + |N(D_{f,e}) \cap   D_{e,f}|}{|D_{e,f}| + |D_{f,e}|},\qquad D_{e,f} = e \setminus f,$$ share non-shared members linked side third hyperedge (\(N(S)\) union hypergraph neighbourhoods \(S\)); \(EO = 0\) \(e = f\). node's coefficient mean EO \(k(k-1)/2\) pairs hyperedges. reduces ordinary clustering coefficient graph count triangles inside hyperedge. "two_node_union", "two_node_min", "two_node_max" – two-mode clustering Latapy, Magnien & Del Vecchio (2008), applied hypernetworks Gallagher & Goldberg (2013): nodes \(u, v\) hyperedge sets \(M(u), M(v)\), \(cc(u, v) = |M(u) \cap M(v)| / |M(u) \cup M(v)|\) (union), \(\min\) / \(\max(|M(u)|, |M(v)|)\) denominator; node's coefficient averages \(cc(u, v)\) hypergraph neighbours \(v\) (Latapy et al.'s \(N(N(u))\)). Undefined values NA. node fewer two projection neighbours "projection" coefficient, node hyperedge "extra_overlap" coefficient (hyperdegree 1 gives 0, Klimm et al. define ), node without neighbours "two_node_*" coefficient. XGI 0.10.2 reports 0 cases; values agree everywhere else (oracle test maps NA 0 comparing). global clustering coefficient \(C_2(H)\) Estrada & Rodriguez-Velazquez (2006) provided (independent oracle). Duplicate hyperedges distinct hyperedges (XGI): raise hyperdegree , "extra_overlap", contribute pairs EO = 0. "extra_overlap" forms dense edge--edge matrix visits every pair intersecting hyperedges, meant hypergraphs thousand hyperedges; variants use sparse products incidence sparse.

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — network_hypergraph
text: net netobject, cograph_network, simplicial_complex, numeric adjacency / weight matrix. Directed inputs symmetrised underlying clique enumerator. p Probability [0, 1] k-clique k >= 3 becomes k-hyperedge. Default 1 (deterministic - every found clique included). type Hyperedge enumeration. "clique" (default) promotes k-cliques binarised adjacency k-hyperedges. metric Vietoris-Rips construction implemented; "vr" / "rips" accepted match.arg raise error rather silently aliasing "clique". include_pairwise Logical. Include 2-edges input network 2-hyperedges. Default TRUE. Set FALSE "fully higher-order" hypergraph containing k-hyperedges k >= 3. max_size Integer >= 2. Maximum hyperedge size extract. Default 3L (triangles ). 4L also includes 4-cliques 4-hyperedges, etc. threshold Numeric. Edge weight cutoff used binarise adjacency clique enumeration. Default 0 (non-zero weight edge). seed Optional integer reproducible Bernoulli sampling 0 < p < 1. x net_hg object (print). n Number rows default table print. Default 10. ... Additional arguments (ignored). object net_hg object (summary).

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — network_hypergraph
text: construction follows Burgio, Matamalas, Gomez & Arenas (2020) simplicial / hypergraph contagion. k-clique k >= 3 found underlying graph (via simplicial()), independent Bernoulli(p) trial decides whether clique becomes k-hyperedge. Underlying pairwise edges always retained include_pairwise = TRUE, resulting hypergraph contains original 2-edge structure sampled higher-order interactions. limits: p = 0 include_pairwise = TRUE reproduces input pairwise network hypergraph size-2 edges. p = 1 include_pairwise = FALSE returns fully higher-order hypergraph containing k-hyperedges (k >= 3) found network's clique complex.

title: Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure — network_hypergraph
code: set.seed(1) n <- 8 adj <- matrix(stats::rbinom(n * n, 1, 0.5), n, n) diag(adj) <- 0 adj <- (adj + t(adj)) > 0 rownames(adj) <- colnames(adj) <- LETTERS[seq_len(n)] hg <- network_hypergraph(adj, p = 1, max_size = 3L) print(hg) #> Hypergraph: 8 nodes, 51 hyperedges (sizes 2: 23, 3: 28) #> Source: network cliques (p = 1.00, include_pairwise = TRUE, max_size = 3) #>  hyperedge size members weight #>         h1    2    C, E     NA #>         h2    2    A, C     NA #>         h3    2    A, D     NA #>         h4    2    D, E     NA #>         h5    2    C, D     NA #>         h6    2    A, B     NA #>         h7    2    B, E     NA #>         h8    2    B, C     NA #>         h9    2    B, H     NA #>        h10    2    D, H     NA #> ... 41 more rows summary(hg) #> Hypergraph summary #>   Nodes:         8 #>   Hyperedges:    51 #>   Mean size:     2.55 #>   Max size:      3

title: Plot a hypergraph with hyperedges as pebbles — plot.net_hg
code: dat <- data.frame(   member = c("a", "b", "c", "b", "c", "d", "d", "e", "f"),   event = c("e1", "e1", "e1", "e2", "e2", "e2", "e3", "e3", "e4") ) hg <- group_hypergraph(dat, "member", "event") plot(hg, color_by = "size", edge_labels = TRUE)  plot(hg, detail = Inf, outline = "fill", alpha = 0.15)  plot(hg, center = c("b", "c"))  plot(hg, dismantled = TRUE)   # disconnected pieces are laid out separately and packed apart <- group_hypergraph(   data.frame(member = c("a", "b", "c", "b", "c", "d", "x", "y", "z"),              event = c("e1", "e1", "e1", "e2", "e2", "e2", "e3", "e3", "e3")),   "member", "event" ) plot(apart, color_by = "size")   # circles sized by how often each node occurs, pointing where it goes next counts <- c(a = 40, b = 25, c = 12, d = 30, e = 5, f = 2) moves <- data.frame(from = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "d", "e"),                     to = c("b", "c", "a", "e", "b", "f"),                     weight = c(20, 9, 4, 8, 3, 1)) plot(hg, node_sizes = counts, direction = moves,      size_title = "occurrences of the node")  plot(hg, node_sizes = counts, direction = moves, transitions = moves,      arrow_style = "outside")   # groups of events with their trial counts: the count colours the pebbles # and writes a title box per group; points sized by how many trials # contain each event members <- data.frame(   group = c("Hint", "Hint", "Hint", "Question", "Question", "Question"),   state = c("Wrong", "Hint", "Retry", "Wrong", "Question", "Retry"),   trials = c(120, 120, 120, 80, 80, 80) ) trial_groups <- group_hypergraph(members, actor = "state", group = "group") event_trials <- data.frame(state = c("Wrong", "Hint", "Question", "Retry"),                            trials = c(200, 120, 80, 190)) plot(trial_groups, node_sizes = event_trials)

title: Windowed Sequence Hyperedges — window_hypergraph
text: Builds hypergraph categorical sequence data: fixed-size window moves sequence distinct states observed inside one window form one hyperedge (Ding et al. 2020). Windows whose distinct state sets coincide collapse single hyperedge whose weight number windows (window_counts); incidence cells hold total within-window occurrences state, incidence matrix carries edge-dependent vertex weights (Chitra & Raphael 2019) hg_cluster() type = "random_walk" uses directly. window counts default hyperedge weights whole Laplacian family (hg_laplacian(), hg_cluster(), hg_classify()).
